title: Boiling mud and a power plant
text: The Coso volcanic field is known for boiling mud pots and fumaroles within an area of many little-eroded volcanoes. Geothermal power began there in 1987, and the field now produces more than 270 megawatts of electricity. Since 1987 it has delivered more than 26,000 gigawatt-hours of electricity. Hot fluids are brought up from the fractured rock below, turned to steam to drive a turbine, and then reinjected into the ground.
